text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: cluster-prod-us-east-1 - ephemeral storage usage > 95% on nodes (ip-10-0-12-41, ip-10-0-12-43). Multiple pods reported OOM/crashloop (serve-runtime). Auto-eviction triggered.

maya (oncall): ack. grabbing logs and starting triage. which services are flapping?

ajay (eng-runtime): seeing repeated container restarts on serve-runtime v2 across 3 pods. Logs show modelcache write errors followed by CUDA init failure during warmup: "CUBLAS_STATUS_INTERNAL_ERROR" then process exits.

lina (eng-sre): I can see nodes with /var/lib/modelcache at 98%. Ephemeral volume is filling with both model artifacts and massive debug logs from runtime crashstack.

maya (oncall): tagging SRE and runtime. @lina @ajay please paste relevant logs.

ajay (eng-runtime): paste logs snippet:
```
E 10:12:03 modelcache: failed to write chunk /var/lib/modelcache/gptx/weights.part: no space left on device
W 10:12:04 runtime: failed to load weights, falling back to stream mode
E 10:12:05 runtime: cuda init error: CUBLAS_STATUS_INTERNAL_ERROR
F 10:12:06 runtime: unhandled exception, exiting
```

sam (support): impact check: error rate on text-generation route jumped to ~6% for Hosted customers in us-east-1, latency spikes to 10s for retries. Two paying customers reported timeouts (support tickets #7891, #7892).

maya (oncall): immediate mitigation plan: 1) stop new model downloads to nodes, 2) free space on hottest nodes by removing stale modelcache entries, 3) cordon one affected node and migrate critical pods to healthy nodes, 4) shift traffic away from us-east-1 if capacity allows.

lina (eng-sre): executing cleanup step. running:
```
kubectl cordon ip-10-0-12-43
kubectl drain ip-10-0-12-43 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
ssh core@ip-10-0-12-41 sudo rm -rf /var/lib/modelcache/tmp_downloads/*
```

ajay (eng-runtime): stopped model prefetcher on the group via config flag, pushed rollback to disable aggressive prefetch: `redwoodctl set-config --group serve-runtime --prefetch=false` (deploy-bot will show).

deploy-bot: config change applied: serve-runtime prefetch=false, rollout id: r-2026-03-15-12

maya (oncall): Lina — any risk to data from deleting tmp_downloads?

lina (eng-sre): tmp_downloads is ephemeral; OK to purge. I will also rotate logs older than 6 hours to compressed files and remove crash stacks beyond 3 days. Running logrotate on nodes: `/etc/cron.daily/logrotate /etc/logrotate.d/serve-runtime` with temporary minsize tweak.

kevin (next-oncall): I'm online and can take over if you want a hand with traffic steering.

maya (oncall): handing off after stabilization. Current state: node ip-10-0-12-43 cordoned and drained; ip-10-0-12-41 had tmp_downloads cleared (~42GB freed). Error rate down from 6% to 1.2% in last 5m. I'll hand to @kevin for watch and follow-ups.

kevin (next-oncall): taking over. immediate follow-ups I will do: 1) add temporary alert to throttle model prefetch concurrency, 2) ensure nodes have eviction thresholds set to 90% for ephemeral, 3) open runbook ticket to cap modelcache disk use per-node.

ajay (eng-runtime): Root cause hypothesis: aggressive parallel model downloads + unrotated verbose crash logs caused ephemeral to saturate during a concurrent model rollout. When write failed, runtime attempted recovery that triggered CUDA re-inits on warm start leading to CUBLAS internal errors and process crashes.

sam (support): Customer comms: posted advisory to affected accounts (tickets #7891/#7892) — advising retry and noting we're mitigating. No data loss.

lina (eng-sre): quick diagnostic commands ran:
```
kubectl top nodes
df -h /var/lib/modelcache
journalctl -u serve-runtime -n 200 | grep -i cublas
```

maya (oncall): marking incident as "mitigating". Creating follow-up tasks: ENG-RUNTIME to add disk quota to modelcache (TBD), ENG-SRE to add alert for modelcache write errors and per-pod disk usage, DevEx to add guardrail on prefetch concurrency for Hosted accounts.

kevin (next-oncall): also routing traffic away from us-east-1 to us-west-2 via routing policy for the next 30m to reduce load on consolidated nodes. executed: `redwoodctl route set --region us-east-1 --weight 70 --backup us-west-2`

ajay (eng-runtime): short-term patch plan: 1) cap concurrent downloads to 2 per node, 2) fail-fast on model download write errors and fallback to smaller model variant, 3) add immediate log level throttling on repeated stack traces. Will follow up with PR.

sam (support): logged customer impact: two enterprise customers saw 10-15 failed requests each, no SLA breaches yet but monitoring for continued spikes.

maya (oncall): last check — error rate stable at ~0.9%, latency returning to normal for most requests. I'll update incident channel and create postmortem ticket. Passing pager to @kevin. :white_check_mark:

kevin (next-oncall): acknowledged handoff. Creating JIRA: RED-INC-2234 "Ephemeral space surge -> modelcache & runtime crash" and adding assignees: ajay, lina. Action items in ticket summary: disk quota, prefetch guardrails, logrotate tuning, alerting for modelcache throughput, postmortem in 2 business days.

ajay (eng-runtime): quick note for postmortem: capture model rollout schedule, any overlapping prefetch config changes, list of affected nodes. I will attach runtime crash traces and proposed PR for cap.

lina (eng-sre): I'll add node-level remediation playbook steps and a script to safely purge modelcache tmp files on pressure.

sam (support): I've sent templated customer updates to affected accounts and set alerts to escalate if error rate >3% for more than 10m.

maya (oncall): closing immediate mitigation. next steps: 1) kevin to lead follow-up, 2) ajay/lina implement changes, 3) support to finalize customer notes, 4) postmortem meeting scheduled. Good work everyone. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: deploy r-2026-03-15-12 rolled back prefetch on serve-runtime (stable).

kevin (next-oncall): taking ownership for post-incident action list. I'll update RED-INC-2234 with timelines and postmortem invite.

maya (oncall): handing off complete, signing out.
